title: Minimum of a rotated sorted array
statement: Return the minimum of a rotated sorted array of distinct integers in O(log n).
hints: Compare mid with the last element: is the minimum to the right of mid?
The predicate nums[i] ≤ nums[last] is false…false true…true; the first true is the minimum.

solution.explanation: Elements ≤ the last element form a suffix (the rotated part, starting at the minimum). So the minimum is the first index where nums[i] ≤ nums[n − 1]: the lower-bound template on a monotone predicate.
solution.python:
def find_min_rotated(nums):
    lo, hi = 0, len(nums) - 1
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if nums[mid] > nums[hi]: lo = mid + 1
        else: hi = mid
    return nums[lo]
